With auto-rotate on, apps that support rotation can also turn 180° when you hold the phone upside down.
Allow third-party apps to open files by default
When a third-party app is selected and \'Always\' is chosen, the system will no longer ignore this choice.
Default sort order for the app list
Sets the sort order in App management. The alphabetical index on the right matches the list only when you sort by name.
Show dots even after app updates
By default, dots appear only on apps newly installed from the app store. To hide the dots, open Home screen icons.
Ask which app to use when no default is set
If you haven’t chosen a default, you’ll be asked which app to open instead of being taken straight to the system’s preset app. This doesn’t change your Home app.
Brightness transition speed during sudden lighting changes
Transition speed for automatic brightness when ambient light changes abruptly. Lowering reduces harsh jumps; increasing makes it more responsive. A system restart is required after changes.
Brightness will not exceed this limit, even in bright surroundings. 100% is the maximum brightness without High Brightness mode. A system restart is required to apply changes.
Brightness will not drop below this limit, even in dark conditions. A system restart is required after changes.
Controls how quickly the screen brightness adjusts to changes in ambient light. 100% is the system default. Higher values result in faster adjustment. A system restart is required to apply changes.
Allow apps to launch each other in the background
Allow all apps if none are selected
Disabling restrictions on apps launching each other in the background may increase battery consumption.
Allow selected apps to read the clipboard in the background
These apps can read the clipboard in the background and may access anything you copy.
Do not automatically archive apps by default
When storage runs low, the system won’t automatically archive apps. Archiving removes the app but keeps its data.
Disables the splash screen on app launch. The screen may remain blank for 1–2 seconds during the transition.
Show language settings for all apps
Shows the App language setting for every app.
Wake the screen if a fingerprint isn\'t recognized
If the screen is off, a failed fingerprint scan will wake it.
Disable the floating window\'s three-dot menu
Disables the menu popup when tapping the three dots at the top of a floating window. Dragging and resizing remain unaffected.
Remember the floating window\'s position and size
After dragging the floating window in vertical mode, it remembers the last position and size when reopening the same app. The position and size are reset after a restart.
Allow 32-bit apps to be installed on 64-bit-only devices.
Allow 1Hz refresh rate at any brightness
Requires a compatible display. The refresh rate can drop to 1 Hz at any brightness. Game Assistant may cause flicker on some models.
Hide compatibility warnings for older apps
Hide warnings when opening apps built for older Android versions, 32-bit-only apps or apps that don’t support the current display size.
The system won’t notify you when an app reads the clipboard, so you may not notice it has accessed what you copied.
Hide Developer Options and debugging from selected apps
Selected apps will see Developer Options, USB debugging and wireless debugging as turned off. Restart the phone to apply.
Extend app content into the front camera cutout area
Content can extend into the front camera cutout and may be obscured. Restart the phone to apply.
Excludes floating windows from other apps in screenshots, screen recordings, and casting. Only affects windows opened after you enable it.
Keep accessibility services running in game mode
In Game Mode, the system no longer disables accessibility services for listed apps.
Keep wireless debugging on when switching between Wi-Fi networks with the same name
Wireless debugging stays on when you switch between routers with the same network name and password. It still turns off if you disconnect from Wi-Fi or join a different network.
Stop the system app store from redirecting store links
Opens the app listing in the store the link points to or in your chosen default store, such as Google Play.
Keep notifications when an app is force-stopped
Keep app notifications in Super power saving mode
Super power saving mode keeps notifications from apps. The mode’s usual background app restrictions still apply.
Keep default settings after installing a new app.
When a new app capable of opening similar content is installed, the previously selected \'Always\' option will not be cleared.
Allow more than 50 notifications for a single app
Remove the 50-notification limit per app. Excessive notifications may slow down the system.
Do not turn on the screen when plugging in or unplugging the charger
Plugging in or unplugging the charger leaves the screen off.
Hold the power button to toggle the flashlight while the screen is off
With this setting on, the screen wakes when you release the power button.
Allow app installs via ADB without confirmation
Installs apps through ADB without showing a confirmation prompt.
Allow Google services to run in the background
Excludes Google services from background restrictions.
Reset manual brightness adjustments when the screen turns off
With auto brightness on, turning the screen off clears your manual adjustment. When you wake the screen, brightness is set according to the ambient light. Restart your phone to apply.
Screen dimming time before automatic screen-off
Calculated as a percentage of the auto screen-off time. -1 keeps the system default, 0 turns off the screen without dimming. A system restart is required after making changes.
Duration for the screen to fade out and turn off. -1 keeps the system default. 0 turns the screen off immediately. Changes require a system restart.
Keep the status bar and gesture guide bar hidden
While an app is in full-screen mode, swiping in from the edge no longer reveals the status bar or gesture guide bar.
Adds the options below to Android’s app pinning feature.
Return to the lock screen immediately after unpinning an app.
Unpin an app by holding the power button
When an app is pinned, holding the power button exits app pinning without opening the power menu.
Allow apps to pin themselves without confirmation
Any app can pin itself without asking you to confirm.
Shows tasks that the system or an app normally hides from Recents. Transparent activities and background screens may also appear.
Set the same display duration for all pop-up messages. Set it to 0 to use the system default.
If you allow only selected apps, Android’s own pop-up messages will still appear.
Use the standard Android power menu
Holding the power button opens the simpler Android power menu in place of the device’s power menu and its extended options.
Use the standard Android screenshot interface
Uses the standard Android screenshot interface. OnePlus features such as scrolling screenshots and editing will be unavailable.

Prevent calls from interrupting the selected app.
When the selected app is playing, incoming calls no longer interrupt its audio, and the app stops receiving call status updates.
Allow the volume button to toggle the flashlight
With the screen off, hold Volume Down to turn the flashlight on or off. The shortcut is unavailable during media playback. You can also turn the flashlight off with the power button.
Leave the selection empty to use this with all players.
Keep media at its current volume
Short sounds, such as notification tones or navigation prompts, will no longer lower the volume of the music you’re playing.
Set the number of volume steps for all audio streams

Increases the number of volume steps proportionally for all audio streams. Restart your phone to apply. Raising the number of steps lowers the current volume. A separate media volume step setting takes precedence.

The percentage stays outside the battery icon and remains visible. If space is limited, Fluid Cloud may overlap the icon.

OShin, an Xposed module for ColorOS, runs an MCP service on my phone. Connect to it to help me review and adjust settings.

Connection
- Protocol: MCP (Streamable HTTP). Send Authorization: Bearer %2$s with every request.
- Choose an address based on where you are running:
· On this phone (Termux, a mobile AI app, etc.): %1$s
· On this computer with the phone connected via USB or wireless debugging: run %3$s, then connect to %1$s.
· %4$s
- If your client only supports stdio MCP servers, use an HTTP-to-stdio bridge such as mcp-remote.
- If you can make HTTP requests but cannot add an MCP server, send a JSON-RPC 2.0 POST to the same address (Content-Type: application/json). Use tools/list to list tools and tools/call to call them with name and arguments in params. You can skip initialize.
- If none of these methods work, for example because you are in the cloud and cannot reach my phone or computer, tell me and stop retrying.
- If the port connects but requests get no response, OShin may be frozen in the background. Ask me to bring OShin to the foreground or follow the Background operation instructions on the MCP service page to allow it to stay running.

Usage
- Call get_status first to check the framework connection, root access, and whether changes are allowed.
- Find features with search_features by title, pinyin, or key, or browse with list_pages and get_page. A feature is identified by its page route and key.
- Change a setting with set_feature. Apply the change by calling restart_scope with the returned restartTargets. Pages with routes starting with android change the system framework and require me to restart the phone.
- If set_feature reports that changes are disabled, ask me to turn on “%5$s” on OShin’s MCP service page.
- To troubleshoot, use list_log_issues for errors and crashes, get_log_issue for stack traces, read_logs for raw logs, and list_modified_features for changed features.
- Change only the settings I explicitly request. Before changing them, explain what will change. Afterward, tell me what changed and which apps restarted.

ctx is read-only. Writes have no effect and throw an error in strict mode. New fields may be added. Existing fields are retained.
• api: JS API version, currently 1.
• slot: slot ID.
• pkg: host package, currently com.android.systemui.
• host.versionCode: SystemUI version code, or 0 in a test run.
• now: intended display time, in milliseconds since the epoch. Date.now() and new Date() without arguments use this value.
• tz: local offset from UTC at now, in minutes. UTC+8 is 480.
• tzNext, tzNextOff: when there is an upcoming daylight saving time change, its timestamp in milliseconds and the offset in minutes after the change.
• lang: system language, such as zh-CN, zh-Hans-CN, or en-US.
• input: slot-specific input, described under Slots.
Local time methods such as Date.getHours may not match tz. Format times with oshin.fmtDate or apply tz yourself. If ctx exceeds 16 KiB, the script is skipped and the original content is shown.

Place a comment header within the first 40 lines. Start it with // ==OShinScript== and end it with // ==/OShinScript==. Use // @key value for each field. Key names are case-insensitive.

Optional fields:

Additional rules:

• Source size limit: 64 KiB in UTF-8.
• Bidirectional text controls are not allowed (U+202A–202E, U+2066–2069, U+200E, U+200F, U+061C), so that the displayed code matches what runs.

Required fields cannot be missing, empty, duplicated, or too long:
• @name: script name, up to 200 characters.
• @id: a UUID generated when you create the script. Uppercase letters are converted to lowercase.
• @version: one to four numeric components. Suffixes such as -beta or +build are allowed, for example 1.0.0 or 2.1-beta.
• @api: use 1. Higher versions require an OShin update.
• @slot: slot ID, listed under Slots.

oshin is a read-only global object. oshin.api is 1. It also provides three functions:
• oshin.fmtDate(ms, pattern): format a numeric millisecond timestamp using ctx.tz. At or after ctx.tzNext it uses tzNextOff. The default pattern is yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss. Call only inside run.
• oshin.pad(n, width): convert n to text and pad it on the left with zeros up to width characters. The default width is 2.
• oshin.fmtRate(bytesPerSecond): format a rate as B/s, KB/s, MB/s, or GB/s using powers of 1024. B/s and values of 100 or more are rounded to whole numbers. Other values use one decimal place. Invalid and negative inputs are treated as 0.

fmtDate groups repeated letters into one pattern:
• yy: two-digit year. Other lengths, including y and yyyy, use the full year.
• M, MM: numeric month. MMM or longer: month name (11月 in Chinese, Nov for MMM and November for MMMM or longer in English).
• d: day of the month. H: hour (0–23). h: hour (1–12). m: minutes. s: seconds. Repeat twice for two digits with a leading zero.
• S: tenths of a second. SS: hundredths. SSS: milliseconds.
• E to EEE: short weekday (周一 or Mon). EEEE or longer: full weekday (星期一 or Monday).
• a: 上午 or 下午 in Chinese, AM or PM in English.
• Single quotes enclose literal text. Two single quotes output one quote. All other characters, including unsupported letters, are copied as written.
• A ctx.lang beginning with zh uses Chinese. All other values use English.

A slot is a place in the interface where JavaScript can change the displayed text, such as the status bar clock. Each script belongs to one slot. It runs in an isolated SystemUI environment, reads the slot input, and returns text. On a timeout, error, or overlong result, the original content is shown.\nThis page describes JS API v%1$d.

To prevent SystemUI slowdowns, each script is subject to these limits:
• Time: see limits per slot; sync slots also have a caller wait limit. Script loading (compiling and executing top-level code) is limited to 200 ms.
• Memory: 4 MiB per script (insufficient memory if exhausted); stack 256 KiB (deep recursion causes errors).
• Single values: strings max 65535 chars, BigInt 8192 bits, array-like length max 1048576, regex source 4096 bytes.
• Output: serialized return value max 4096 bytes. Control chars (except line breaks) and Bidi controls are removed; line endings normalized. Slot checks line/char count (excluding line breaks); exceeding limits counts as one failure, content remains unchanged.
• Power: if JS CPU time exceeds 200 ms within 60 seconds, calls are throttled (suspended) and auto-resume.

A script is disabled automatically in any of these cases. Its slot then shows the original content until reset:
• Three timeouts in 10 minutes. A timeout counts only if CPU time reaches at least 80% of the limit. Delays caused by a busy device do not count.
• Five consecutive failures. A successful call resets this count.
• One out-of-memory error. A script that executes throw null also counts.
To resume, choose Re-enable scripts in the script center or assign a corrected script.

Two additional safeguards:\n• Disable all scripts: turn on this option in the Script Center to restore the original content in every slot immediately. Installed scripts and slot assignments are kept.\n• Safe mode: if SystemUI exits unexpectedly twice in a row during the same boot session, each time within 60 seconds of loading scripts, all scripts are paused. Stop using or fix the suspected script, then leave safe mode in the Script Center. Re-enable scripts also exits safe mode.
Asynchronous: calculate in the background and display the result when ready, without blocking the interface.

Precomputed: prepare the text for its intended display time, then use the cached result. If no result is ready (for example, just after the screen turns on), calculate it synchronously once and wait up to %1$d ms.

Synchronous: wait up to %1$d ms for a result, then fall back to the original content. After three missed deadlines in one minute, pause calls for 60 seconds. Identical input is evaluated only once per second.

Use a classic script with a global function run(ctx), not an ES module. The function runs whenever text is needed. Its return value determines what appears:
• A string replaces the text. An empty string is valid.
• null or undefined preserves the original text and does not count as an error.
• An exception or any other return type, such as a number or object, counts as a failure and preserves the original text.

Execution rules:
• Return synchronously. An async function, a returned Promise or thenable, or an unfinished Promise counts as an error. Timers such as setTimeout and setInterval are unavailable.
• Top-level code runs once when loaded, with a 200 ms limit. ctx is unavailable then. Date.now(), new Date() without arguments, Date(), and oshin.fmtDate will throw. Read the time, time zone, and language inside run.
• Globals persist between SystemUI calls and can cache data, but switching scripts, automatic shutdown, re-enabling, or restarting SystemUI clears them.
• Use ctx.now for time. Precomputed slots can calculate future text out of order, so do not store the previous time in a global variable.
• Each editor test run starts fresh and allows 1 second for diagnostics. Use Run once in SystemUI to check actual behavior.

Scripts run in a QuickJS sandbox. Available standard objects include Object, Array, String, Number, Boolean, Symbol, Math, JSON, Date, RegExp, Map, Set, BigInt, Reflect, and Error. Promise exists, but run must return synchronously.
Unavailable features:
• eval and the Function, AsyncFunction, GeneratorFunction, and AsyncGeneratorFunction constructors throw when called.
• Proxy, WeakRef, TypedArray (including Int8Array), SharedArrayBuffer, Atomics, Intl, and performance.
• Timers, import, require, and any module loading.
• Network, file, interprocess communication, Java, reflection, and other system APIs.
• Modifying oshin or console. Both are frozen.

Customize the carrier name at the top of Control Center and the notification drawer.

ctx.input fields: text (the original carrier label), anySimReady (whether any SIM is ready), airplaneMode (whether airplane mode is on), and dataUsage. For two SIMs, text might be “China Mobile | China Unicom”. The separator varies by system version. dataUsage is only nonempty when the system shows data usage. In that case, usage replaces both the carrier name and script output. With no SIM, in airplane mode, or when the original text is empty, the script is skipped and the system text is shown. Return 1 line of up to 24 characters to replace the entire label. An empty string hides it. Returning null or missing the 4 ms synchronous deadline restores the original label, or the custom carrier name if set. For time, use ctx.now or oshin.fmtDate(ctx.now, …).
Customize the status bar clock display, for example by adding the date or changing the time format.

ctx.input fields: is24h (system 24-hour setting), showSeconds (OShin’s clock setting if clock customization is on, otherwise the system setting), dualRow (whether text has two lines), and text (the existing OShin clock text, or system text if customization is off). Use ctx.now, a millisecond timestamp, and format it with oshin.fmtDate(ctx.now, \'HH:mm:ss\'). Do not cache the time: the result is calculated ahead of its display time. Return up to 2 lines and 32 characters within 20 ms to replace the clock, or null to keep text. Script mode updates on whole seconds. It cannot display milliseconds.
Customize the status bar hardware indicators, for example the format used for power or temperature.

ctx.input fields:
• kind: power / temp / extra for indicators 1 / 2 / 3. slot: number from 1 to 3. charging: charging status. watt (W), currentMa (mA), voltage (V), batteryLevel (%).
• batteryTempC, cpuTempC, gpuTempC, skinTempC: temperatures in °C. cpuFreqMhz: highest core frequency. cpuClusterFreqMhz: array of cluster frequencies, from little to big cores.
• cpuUsage (%), cpuCoreUsage (array of per-core loads), gpuUsage (%), ramUsage (%), ramUsedGb, swapUsage (%), refreshRate (Hz), netDownBps and netUpBps (bytes per second).
• line1 and line2: the two formatted lines for the selected readings. chargerVoltage (V), chargerPower (theoretical power, W), batteryHealth (%), chargerType (fast-charging protocol), inputCurrent (A), cycleCount, fullCapacityMah and remainCapacityMah (full and current capacity, mAh).
Unavailable values are null, except watt, currentMa, voltage, batteryTempC, cpuTempC, cpuFreqMhz, cpuUsage, ramUsage, netDownBps, and netUpBps, which are 0 when unavailable. Return up to 2 lines and 48 characters to replace the whole text, or null to keep the selected readings.
